claim: Fluid flows generated by motile cilia guide the establishment of the left-right asymmetry of the body in the vertebrate left-right organizer.
source: Fluid flows generated by motile cilia are guiding the establishment of the left-right asymmetry of the body in the vertebrate left-right organizer.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise of the study.

claim: The number of immotile cilia is too small to ensure robust left and right determination by mechanosensing, given the large spatial variability of the flow.
source: Our results show that the number of immotile cilia is too small to ensure robust left and right determination by mechanosensing, given the large spatial variability of the flow.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and supported by computational modeling and experimental data on cilia counts and flow variability.

claim: Motile cilia could sense their own motion by a yet unknown mechanism.
source: However, motile cilia could sense their own motion by a yet unknown mechanism.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a possibility based on theoretical analysis.

claim: Transport of chemical signals by the flow can provide a simple and reliable mechanism of asymmetry establishment.
source: Finally, transport of chemical signals by the flow can provide a simple and reliable mechanism of asymmetry establishment.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the abstract and supported by computational simulations of particle diffusion.

claim: In most vertebrate species, LR axis determination is set by a symmetry biasing event which is under the control of a directional flow generated by the chiral beating pattern of motile cilia.
source: In most of the vertebrate species, LR axis determination is set by a symmetry biasing event which is under the control of a directional flow generated by the chiral beating pattern of motile cilia (Hirokawa et al., 2009; Nakamura and Hamada, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The molecular mechanisms of LR axis determination are highly conserved from fish, amphibians to mammals.
source: To date, even though the molecular mechanisms of LR axis determination are highly conserved from fish, amphibians to mammals (Blum et al., 2014a), many steps of this process are not yet understood (Ferreira and Vermot, 2017; Shinohara and Hamada, 2017; Wolpert, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The LRO is a transient structure and its function is required for a limited period of time.
source: The LRO is a transient structure and its function is required for a limited period of time.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of the LRO.

claim: In zebrafish, the LRO is visible between 10 hr after fertilization (3-somite stage) and 16 hr after fertilization (14-somite stage).
source: In zebrafish, the LRO is visible between 10 hr after fertilization (3-somite stage) and 16 hr after fertilization (14-somite stage) (Essner et al., 2005; Yuan et al., 2015).
evidence: This timing is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Cilia generate a directed flow by beating in a spatially asymmetric fashion.
source: Cilia generate a directed flow by beating in a spatially asymmetric fashion (Satir and Christensen, 2007).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Cilia in the LRO are relatively short and their beating pattern resembles rotation along the mantle of a tilted cone.
source: Cilia in the LRO are relatively short and their beating pattern resembles rotation along the mantle of a tilted cone (Hirokawa et al., 2006; Nonaka et al., 2005; Okada et al., 2005).
evidence: This description is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Spatial orientation is a key functional feature of motile cilia involved in LR symmetry breaking, as it determines the strength and directionality of the induced flow.
source: Spatial orientation is, therefore, a key functional feature of motile cilia involved in LR symmetry breaking, as it determines the strength and directionality of the induced flow (Cartwright et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The molecular mechanisms that set cilia orientation involve elements of the Planar Cell Polarity (PCP) pathway as well as flow itself.
source: The molecular mechanisms that set this orientation involve elements of the Planar Cell Polarity (PCP) pathway (Borovina et al., 2010; Hashimoto et al., 2010; Song et al., 2010) as well as flow itself (Guirao et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The sense of cilia rotation is determined by the chirality of the structure of their protein building blocks.
source: This paradigm works well with cilia, as the sense of cilia rotation is determined by the chirality of the structure of their protein building blocks (Hilfinger and Jülicher, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: According to the chemosensing hypothesis, the directional flow establishes a LR asymmetric chemical gradient that is detected by signaling systems which leads to LR asymmetric gene expression and cell responses in the LRO.
source: According to the chemosensing hypothesis, the directional flow establishes a LR asymmetric chemical gradient that is detected by signaling systems which leads to LR asymmetric gene expression and cell responses in the LRO (Okada et al., 2005).
evidence: This hypothesis is described with a citation to previous research.

claim: The mechanosensing hypothesis proposes that the LRO cells can detect the mechanical effects of flow.
source: The mechanosensing hypothesis, on the other hand, proposes that the LRO cells can detect the mechanical effects of flow.
evidence: This hypothesis is described as an alternative to chemosensing.

claim: Mechanosensing is mediated by a particular type of sensory cilia that is able to trigger a local, asymmetric response of the so-called crown cells, which are located at the periphery of the node (mouse LRO).
source: It has been suggested that this mechanosensing is mediated by a particular type of sensory cilia that is able to trigger a local, asymmetric response of the so-called crown cells, which are located at the periphery of the node (mouse LRO) (McGrath et al., 2003; Tabin and Vogan, 2003).
evidence: This mechanism is described with citations to previous research.

claim: In the zebrafish LRO, the model for cilia-mediated mechanotransduction suggests that sensing cilia are immotile and will activate a cellular response due to physical asymmetries generated by the flow.
source: In the zebrafish LRO (also called Kupffer's vesicle or KV), the model for cilia-mediated mechanotransduction suggests that sensing cilia are immotile and will activate a cellular response due to physical asymmetries generated by the flow (Sampaio et al., 2014).
evidence: This model is described with a citation to previous research.

claim: Proper asymmetry establishment occurs even in mutant mice with only two motile cilia in the LRO.
source: The flow detection apparatus needs to be remarkably efficient, as demonstrated by the observation that, despite wild-type mice having hundreds of motile cilia in their LRO, proper asymmetry establishment occurs even in mutant mice with only two motile cilia in the LRO (Shinohara et al., 2012).
evidence: This observation is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Correct asymmetry establishment occurs in zebrafish mutants with only 30 motile cilia.
source: Similarly, although wild-type zebrafish usually has around 50–60 motile cilia in the KV, correct asymmetry establishment occurs in zebrafish mutants with only 30 motile cilia (Sampaio et al., 2014).
evidence: This observation is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Motile cilia might be chemosensors.
source: Considering that motile cilia might be chemosensors (Shah et al., 2009), LR symmetry breaking could rely on a combination of both mechanosensory and chemosensory mechanisms that could work in parallel.
evidence: This possibility is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The molecular nature of a possible diffusing compound involved in chemosensing is still not known.
source: To date, however, several issues with both hypotheses have emerged: the molecular nature of a possible diffusing compound involved is still not known (Freund et al., 2012; Shinohara and Hamada, 2017)
evidence: This gap in knowledge is stated with citations to previous research.

claim: Cilia-mediated mechanotransduction in the mouse node has recently been experimentally challenged.
source: and cilia-mediated mechanotransduction in the mouse node has recently been experimentally challenged (Delling et al., 2016).
evidence: This challenge is supported by a citation to recent research.

claim: The directional flow in the zebrafish KV corresponds to an anti-clockwise rotation around the dorsoventral (DV) axis when viewed from the dorsal pole of the Kupffer's vesicle.
source: In the zebrafish embryo, the directional flow corresponds to an anti-clockwise rotation around the dorsoventral (DV) axis when viewed from the dorsal pole of the Kupffer's vesicle (KV) (Figure 1A) (Essner et al., 2005; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005).
evidence: This flow pattern is described with citations to previous research and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The directional flow depends on two main topological features of the vesicle: a profile of cilia density and a cilia orientation pattern following a meridional tilt in the KV.
source: This theoretical analysis shows that the directional flow depends on two main topological features of the vesicle: a profile of cilia density and a cilia orientation pattern following a meridional tilt in the KV.
evidence: This conclusion is derived from theoretical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The average density of cilia did not display any significant differences between left and right sides of the KV.
source: We found that the average density of cilia did not display any significant differences between left and right sides of the KV (Figure 3B).
evidence: This finding is based on analysis of 20 vesicles with 1197 cilia and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A steep density gradient was observed along the AP axis, with increasing density towards the anterior pole of the vesicle (about four times denser than posterior).
source: As expected from previous studies (Wang et al., 2011, 2012), a steep density gradient was observed along the AP axis, with increasing density towards the anterior pole of the vesicle (about four times denser than posterior) (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This gradient is observed in the data and consistent with previous studies cited.

claim: A gradient of cilia density was also seen along the DV axis, albeit shallower (dorsal being two times denser than ventral).
source: Interestingly, a gradient of cilia density was also seen along the DV axis, albeit shallower (dorsal being two times denser than ventral) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This gradient is observed in the data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The dominant AP density gradient would lead to a significant contribution to directional flows around the AP axis, which are not observed.
source: Together, these results rule out scenario 1, since the dominant AP density gradient would lead to a significant contribution to directional flows around the AP axis, which are not observed (Supatto et al., 2008).
evidence: This inference is based on the observed density gradient and citation to previous research showing no AP-directed flows.

claim: The θ tilt of the average cilium is near 46° and the average cilium has a 14° φ angle.
source: Despite a relatively broad distribution of cilia orientations (r= 0.76), we found that the θ tilt of the average cilium is near 46° and the average cilium has a 14° φ angle (Figure 3C).
evidence: This measurement is based on analysis of 1013 motile cilia and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: 65% of all motile cilia exhibited a φ angle between −45° and +45° (meridional quadrant).
source: In total, 65% of all motile cilia exhibited a φ angle between −45° and +45° (meridional quadrant).
evidence: This percentage is calculated from the analysis of 1013 motile cilia.

claim: Motile cilia are oriented on average with a meridional tilt and support scenario 2.
source: These data demonstrate that motile cilia are oriented on average with a meridional tilt and support scenario 2 (Figure 2B), in which cilia meridional tilt is the dominant mechanism generating the directional flow within the KV (Figure 2C).
evidence: This conclusion is based on the orientation data and theoretical analysis.

claim: With such a meridional tilt, all motile cilia can contribute to the directional flow around the DV axis, wherever they are located within the KV.
source: With such a meridional tilt, all motile cilia can contribute to the directional flow around the DV axis, wherever they are located within the KV.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed meridional tilt pattern.

claim: During the developmental time window from 3-SS to 9-14-SS, the KV size drastically changes with an average volume increasing from 17 pl at early to 45 pl and 82 pl at mid and late stages.
source: During this developmental time window, the KV size drastically changes with an average volume increasing from 17 pl at early to 45 pl and 82 pl at mid and late stages.
evidence: This measurement is based on analysis of multiple embryos at different stages.

claim: The average number of cilia per vesicle increases from 30 at early, to 52 and 63 at mid and late stages.
source: The average number of cilia per vesicle also increases from 30 at early, to 52 and 63 at mid and late stages (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Table 1).
evidence: This measurement is based on analysis of multiple embryos at different stages and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Table 1.

claim: The fraction of motile cilia increases with time (44% of immotile cilia per vesicle on average at 3-SS vs. 2% at 8-SS).
source: Not surprisingly, the ratio of motile versus non-motile cilia also changes along with the total number, as previously observed by (Yuan et al., 2015). The fraction of motile cilia increases with time (44% of immotile cilia per vesicle on average at 3-SS vs. 2% at 8-SS) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and Table 1).
evidence: This measurement is based on analysis of multiple embryos at different stages, consistent with previous research cited.

claim: At mid and late stages, a steep gradient of cilia surface density along the AP axis is observed, which is not yet established at 3-SS.
source: At mid and late stages, we observed a steep gradient of cilia surface density along the AP axis, which is not yet established at 3-SS (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This observation is based on analysis of cilia density maps at different developmental stages.

claim: A DV gradient of cilia density is present at 3-SS.
source: Instead, a DV gradient of cilia density is present at 3-SS.
evidence: This observation is based on analysis of cilia density maps at 3-SS.

claim: The average orientation angle θ of the motile cilia increases over time (from 32° to 50°).
source: Additionally, it seems that the average orientation angle θ of the motile cilia increases over time (from 32° to 50°, Figure 4A).
evidence: This measurement is based on analysis of cilia orientations at different developmental stages.

claim: Motile cilia at 3-SS already exhibit a clear meridional tilt, as the angle φ of the average motile cilium is close to 0° (57% of all cilia exhibited a φ angle in the meridional quadrant [−45°, +45°]) and θ is high (32°).
source: When focusing on 3-SS embryos, we found that motile cilia at this stage already exhibit a clear meridional tilt, as the angle φ of the average motile cilium is close to 0° (57% of all cilia exhibited a φ angle in the meridional quadrant [−45°, +45°]) and θ is high (32°) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This measurement is based on analysis of cilia orientations at 3-SS.

claim: The few motile cilia at 3-SS are already well oriented and generate a flow of low amplitude but in the proper direction.
source: Together, these data suggest that the few motile cilia at 3-SS are already well oriented and generate a flow of low amplitude but in the proper direction.
evidence: This inference is based on the orientation data and flow calculations at 3-SS.

claim: The flow amplitude increases over time with the most pronounced increase in the anterior region.
source: As expected, due to the increase in anterior cilia density, the flow amplitude increases over time (Figure 4B and Figure 6A) with the most pronounced increase in the anterior region.
evidence: This observation is based on flow calculations at different developmental stages.

claim: In 8-SS and 9–14-SS embryos, the rotational flow persistently points in one direction.
source: Our results consistently show that in 8-SS and 9–14-SS embryos, the rotational flow persistently points in one direction.
evidence: This observation is based on calculation of effective angular velocity at different developmental stages.

claim: In 5 out of 8 vesicles, the flow direction is already set at 3-SS.
source: Most importantly, in 5 out of 8 vesicles, the flow direction is already set at 3-SS (Figure 4C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that directional flow can emerge as early as 3-SS, even though the flow is of low amplitude (Video 2).
evidence: This observation is based on calculation of effective angular velocity at 3-SS.

claim: The establishment of an AP gradient of cilia from 3- to 8-SS does not affect the flow direction.
source: As a consequence, the establishment of an AP gradient of cilia from 3- to 8-SS does not affect the flow direction, which further supports cilia meridional tilt as the dominant mechanism used to generate directional flow within the KV.
evidence: This inference is based on the observation that flow direction is established before the AP gradient develops.

claim: Cilia density and orientation are very variable from embryo to embryo.
source: We first analyzed cilia density in individual vesicles and found that cilia density and orientation are very variable from embryo to embryo (Figure 6B–D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C and Table 1).
evidence: This observation is based on analysis of individual vesicles.

claim: There is strong variability in the local flow velocities between individual vesicles at every developmental stage.
source: We assessed the general amplitude of the flow and found strong variability in the local flow velocities between individual vesicles at every developmental stage (Figure 6B–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This observation is based on flow calculations for individual vesicles.

claim: The calculated profiles reveal a high level of variability of the difference between left and right flow amplitudes, without a persistent bias.
source: In particular, the calculated profiles reveal a high level of variability of the difference between left and right flow amplitudes, without a persistent bias (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This observation is based on flow calculations for individual vesicles.

claim: The maximum velocity at the anterior and posterior poles of the KV is variable from embryo to embryo.
source: Similarly, we found the maximum velocity at the anterior and posterior poles of the KV is variable from embryo to embryo (Figure 6B–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This observation is based on flow calculations for individual vesicles.

claim: The local flow amplitude itself cannot be a good indicator of the embryonic side and is too variable to serve as a robust predictor of the left and right side of the vesicle.
source: We conclude that the local flow amplitude itself cannot be a good indicator of the embryonic side and is too variable to serve as a robust predictor of the left and right side of the vesicle.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observed variability in flow amplitudes.

claim: The directional flow is the most robust left-right asymmetric feature in the vesicle.
source: This identifies the directional flow as the most robust left-right asymmetric feature in the vesicle.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the comparison of flow amplitude variability versus directional flow robustness.

claim: The instantaneous torques show a broad distribution and have a direction opposite to that of the directional flow in about 25% of the cases.
source: The instantaneous torques (dotted lines) show a broad distribution and have a direction opposite to that of the directional flow in about 25% of the cases.
evidence: This observation is based on computational modeling of torques on immotile cilia.

claim: The strong local flow perturbations caused by beating of adjacent cilia induce on average an oscillating torque with an r.m.s amplitude of 9 × 10−19 Nm.
source: These fluctuations are caused by the beating of adjacent cilia, which induces on average an oscillating torque with an r.m.s amplitude of 9 × 10−19 Nm.
evidence: This calculation is based on computational modeling of flow around cilia.

claim: The torques are of a similar order of magnitude as the thermal fluctuations acting on the cilium, whose r.m.s. amplitude is estimated as 2 × 10−19 Nm.
source: Additionally, the torques are of a similar order of magnitude as the thermal fluctuations acting on the cilium, whose r.m.s. amplitude we estimate as 2 × 10−19 Nm (Appendix B).
evidence: This estimate is based on theoretical calculation.

claim: Both the thermal and oscillatory noise can be suppressed by temporal averaging (low-pass filtering) the signal with a time constant longer than 2 s.
source: A simple estimate shows that both the thermal and oscillatory noise can be suppressed by temporal averaging (low-pass filtering) the signal with a time constant longer than 2 s.
evidence: This is an inference based on theoretical analysis of noise suppression.

claim: A sensitivity threshold of 2 × 10−19 Nm would be sufficient to achieve a reliability of 95% in vesicles with the generated distributions.
source: A sensitivity threshold of 2 × 10−19 Nm would be sufficient to achieve a reliability of 95% (less than 5% of the immotile cilia on the left side would not detect the posterior-directed flow) in vesicles with the generated distributions (Figure 7B, dashed lines)
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational modeling of torques on immotile cilia.

claim: The greater variability of experimentally characterized vesicles does not allow 95% reliability (about 10% of the cilia are subject to flows of the opposite directionality).
source: but the greater variability of experimentally characterized vesicles does not allow this level of reliability (about 10% of the cilia are subject to flows of the opposite directionality, Figure 7C, dashed lines).
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational modeling using experimentally characterized vesicles.

claim: For robust flow sensing, three cilia on each side are necessary.
source: For robust flow sensing, we found that three cilia on each side are necessary.
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational modeling of ensemble averaging of torques.

claim: For a 6 μm long cilium the threshold torque corresponds to a shear rate of 0.5 s−1 (shear stress 0.5 mPa).
source: We find that for a 6 μm long cilium the threshold torque corresponds to a shear rate of 0.5 s−1 (shear stress 0.5 mPa).
evidence: This calculation is based on computational modeling.

claim: In renal cilia, calcium signals were observed with shear stresses of 20 mPa and higher.
source: In renal cilia, Rydholm and colleagues (Rydholm et al., 2010) observed calcium signals with shear stresses of 20 mPa and higher.
evidence: This comparison is based on a citation to previous research.

claim: The mechanosensory detection of flow would require cilia with an ability of direction-sensitive flow detection with a threshold 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than known comparable mechanosensory cilia.
source: These results indicate that the mechanosensory detection of flow would require cilia with an ability of direction-sensitive flow detection with a threshold 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than known comparable mechanosensory cilia.
evidence: This conclusion is based on comparison of calculated thresholds with known mechanosensory systems.

claim: Many KV have fewer than three immotile cilia on each side, the number that would be needed for ensemble-averaging to overcome spatial inhomogeneities of the flow.
source: Moreover, many KV have fewer than three immotile cilia on each side, the number that would be needed for ensemble-averaging to overcome spatial inhomogeneities of the flow.
evidence: This observation is based on experimental data on immotile cilia counts.

claim: The number of immotile cilia is higher at 3-SS, but the weaker and less regular flow excludes reliable side detection at that stage.
source: The number of immotile cilia is higher at 3-SS, but the weaker and less regular flow excludes reliable side detection at that stage (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data and computational modeling at 3-SS.

claim: A mechanism of symmetry breaking based solely on mechanical sensing of directional flow appears incompatible with in vivo analysis.
source: Combined with the related finding that cilia from isolated mouse cells do not bend significantly in response to flow applied at endogenous flow amplitudes (Delling et al., 2016), we conclude that a mechanism of symmetry breaking based solely on mechanical sensing of directional flow appears incompatible with our in vivo analysis.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the computational modeling results and citation to experimental findings in mouse.

claim: The mean torque exerted by the fluid on a meridionally tilted beating cilium has the opposite direction from the torque exerted by the directional flow on an immotile cilium.
source: The mean torque exerted by the fluid on a meridionally tilted beating cilium has the opposite direction from the torque exerted by the directional flow on an immotile cilium.
evidence: This is based on computational modeling of torques on motile versus immotile cilia.

claim: A prediction of the auto-sensing hypothesis is that an artificially induced counter-rotating flow (clockwise in dorsal view) would enhance, rather than reverse, the LR difference.
source: A prediction of this auto-sensing hypothesis is therefore that an artificially induced counter-rotating flow (clockwise in dorsal view) would enhance, rather than reverse, the LR difference.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the auto-sensing hypothesis.

claim: Results in the mouse node showing that externally imposed flow of opposite directionality can cause asymmetry reversal contradict the auto-sensing hypothesis.
source: Results in the mouse node (Nonaka et al., 2002) showing that externally imposed flow of opposite directionality can cause asymmetry reversal, contradict this view.
evidence: This contradiction is based on citation to experimental findings in mouse.

claim: The laterality mechanism breaks down in Xenopus when the fluid is made viscoelastic, which brings the directional flow to a halt, even though the cilia are still motile.
source: Another observation in Xenopus that cannot be explained by the auto-sensing hypothesis is that the laterality mechanism breaks down when the fluid is made viscoelastic, which brings the directional flow to a halt, even though the cilia are still motile (Schweickert et al., 2007).
evidence: This observation is based on citation to experimental findings in Xenopus.

claim: Asymmetric transport of signaling molecules in the KV is a much more robust strategy than sensing mechanical cues.
source: Conversely, our numerical simulations show that asymmetric transport of signaling molecules in the KV is a much more robust strategy than sensing mechanical cues.
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational simulations of particle diffusion.

claim: The chemosensory mechanism requires the particle size to be bigger than 2 nm to work.
source: We characterize here the physical limit on the size of the signaling molecule for its reliable asymmetric distribution. Our calculations show that such mechanism requires the particle size to be bigger than 2 nm to work.
evidence: This limit is determined by computational simulations of particle diffusion.

claim: For signaling particles with a Stokes radius of 2 nm, a robust asymmetric readout is obtained in 18 of 20 vesicles.
source: For signaling particles with a Stokes radius of 2 nm, we obtain a robust asymmetric readout in 18 of 20 vesicles.
evidence: This result is based on computational simulations on 20 experimentally characterized vesicles.

claim: For particle sizes of 2–10 nm, more than 95% of the vesicles fulfill the asymmetry requirement.
source: In addition, we performed the computation on a larger number of randomly generated vesicles and see that, for particle sizes of 2–10 nm, more than 95% of the vesicles fulfill the asymmetry requirement.
evidence: This result is based on computational simulations on randomly generated vesicles.

claim: A scenario with cilia distributed homogenously around the whole vesicle is equally efficient for asymmetric transport.
source: Figure 7J shows a scenario with cilia distributed homogenously around the whole vesicle, which is equally efficient.
evidence: This result is based on computational simulations with alternative cilia distributions.

claim: With half the number of cilia (Nc=35), the vesicles still show sufficient average asymmetry, but fail to achieve 95% reliability.
source: With half the number of cilia (Nc=35, Figure 7K) the vesicles still show sufficient average asymmetry, but fail to achieve 95% reliability.
evidence: This result is based on computational simulations with reduced cilia numbers.

claim: The mechanism becomes dysfunctional with 20 motile cilia, which is very close to the minimum observed in vivo.
source: Interestingly, the mechanism becomes dysfunctional with 20 motile cilia, which is very close to the minimum observed in vivo by (Sampaio et al., 2014) (Figure 7L).
evidence: This result is based on computational simulations with reduced cilia numbers and comparison to experimental observations.

claim: The KV contains enough motile cilia to allow robust symmetry establishment through asymmetric transport of signaling molecules, but not much more than needed.
source: This indicates that 'flow-mediated transport of a secreted signaling molecule' is plausible in the KV and that the KV contains enough motile cilia to allow robust symmetry establishment through asymmetric transport of signaling molecules, but not much more than needed.
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational simulations showing the mechanism fails with fewer cilia than observed in vivo.

claim: The physical limits to the reliability of mechanical sensing of flow are stronger than the ones associated with chemical sensing.
source: Our results show that the physical limits to the reliability of mechanical sensing of flow are stronger than the ones associated with chemical sensing and suggest that chemosensation is the key mechanism for LR axis determination.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Results section based on the computational modeling results.

claim: 90–95% of the zebrafish embryos have a properly positioned left axis.
source: Given that 90–95% of the zebrafish embryos have a properly positioned left axis (Gokey et al., 2016), the mechanism eliciting LR bias has to be highly robust even though the KV size, which affects LR patterning, is variable across embryos (Gokey et al., 2016).
evidence: This statistic is cited from previous research.

claim: The KV size affects LR patterning and is variable across embryos.
source: Given that 90–95% of the zebrafish embryos have a properly positioned left axis (Gokey et al., 2016), the mechanism eliciting LR bias has to be highly robust even though the KV size, which affects LR patterning, is variable across embryos (Gokey et al., 2016).
evidence: This relationship is cited from previous research.

claim: Less than 5% of cilia were immotile at 8-SS and 9-14-SS stages.
source: We observed in vivo that the number of immotile cilia decreases over time along with an increase in the number of motile cilia, resulting in a stronger flow velocity and directionality. Nevertheless, the stage at which the number of immotile cilia is high corresponds to the stage where flow is the lowest and the least robust. At later stages, when it directionally is established, we observed that only 5% of cilia were immotile, less than three on each side.
evidence: This observation is based on experimental data at different developmental stages.

claim: The number of immotile cilia is too low to sense the flow direction.
source: The number of immotile cilia is therefore too low to sense the flow direction.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation that fewer than three immotile cilia are present on each side at later stages.

claim: The average distance from one cilium to its nearest neighbor is under 8 µm in the KV.
source: Indeed, the average distance from one cilium to its nearest neighbor is under 8 µm in the KV.
evidence: This measurement is based on experimental data.

claim: At a distance under 8 µm, the strong local flow perturbations have been shown to be chaotic.
source: At such a distance, the strong local flow perturbations have been shown to be chaotic (Supatto et al., 2008).
evidence: This observation is cited from previous research.

claim: The required sensitivity for flow detection is of the same order of magnitude as thermal fluctuations.
source: In addition, the required sensitivity is of the same order of magnitude as thermal fluctuations.
evidence: This comparison is based on theoretical calculations.

claim: The observed average velocities are below the detection threshold found in other mechanosensitive cilia.
source: The observed average velocities are still below the detection threshold found in other mechanosensitive cilia (Delling et al., 2016; Goetz et al., 2014; Nauli et al., 2008; Rydholm et al., 2010)
evidence: This comparison is based on citations to previous research on mechanosensitive cilia.

claim: Small flow velocities are a major challenge to the reliable sensing of directionality.
source: We conclude that small flow velocities are a major challenge to the reliable sensing of directionality.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the comparison of observed velocities with known detection thresholds.

claim: The hypothesis that cilia are capable of directional flow sensing remains untested in vivo.
source: Moreover, the hypothesis that cilia are capable of directional flow sensing remains untested in vivo (Shinohara and Hamada, 2017).
evidence: This gap in knowledge is cited from a review.

claim: Due to spatial inhomogeneities resulting from the cilia distribution, temporal averaging within a single cilium could not be sufficient for robust side determination via detection of flow direction.
source: In addition, we showed that due to spatial inhomogeneities resulting from the cilia distribution, temporal averaging within a single cilium could not be sufficient for robust side determination via detection of flow direction.
evidence: This conclusion is based on computational modeling of flow variability.

claim: Signals from several cilia on each side would need to be ensemble-averaged for robust flow sensing.
source: Signals from several cilia on each side would need to be ensemble-averaged.
evidence: This requirement is inferred from the computational modeling results.

claim: The stage at which the number of immotile cilia is high corresponds to the stage where flow is the lowest and the least robust.
source: Nevertheless, the stage at which the number of immotile cilia is high corresponds to the stage where flow is the lowest and the least robust.
evidence: This observation is based on experimental data at different developmental stages.

claim: Cilia from isolated mouse cells do not bend significantly in response to flow applied at endogenous flow amplitudes.
source: Combined with the related finding that cilia from isolated mouse cells do not bend significantly in response to flow applied at endogenous flow amplitudes (Delling et al., 2016)
evidence: This finding is cited from recent experimental research.

claim: An artificially induced counter-rotating flow can cause asymmetry reversal in the mouse node.
source: Results in the mouse node (Nonaka et al., 2002) showing that externally imposed flow of opposite directionality can cause asymmetry reversal
evidence: This experimental result is cited from previous research.

claim: The particle size range of 2 nm is in the size range of membrane-bound extra cellular vesicles (ECVs).
source: Interestingly, this is in the size range of membrane-bound extra cellular vesicles (ECVs).
evidence: This comparison is based on knowledge of ECV sizes.

claim: ECVs play important roles in intercellular communication and may mediate a wide range of physiological and pathological processes.
source: ECVs play important roles in intercellular communication and may mediate a wide range of physiological and pathological processes (Cocucci et al., 2009; Hogan et al., 2009; Raposo and Stoorvogel, 2013; Wood et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The small number of immotile cilia found in the KV cannot be sufficient to robustly detect the direction of the flow given its high local variability.
source: We show that the small number of immotile cilia found in the KV cannot be sufficient to robustly detect the direction of the flow given its high local variability.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion based on the computational modeling results.

claim: Motile cilia could sense the torques exerted by the fluid as a result of their own motion, which largely surpass the influence of the directional flow.
source: Motile cilia could sense the torques exerted by the fluid as a result of their own motion, which largely surpass the influence of the directional flow.
evidence: This possibility is stated in the Discussion based on computational modeling.

claim: The auto-sensing mechanism is incompatible with findings in other vertebrate species in which laterality establishment was suppressed in viscoelastic fluids and reversed with an artificial flow.
source: However, this mechanism is incompatible with findings in other vertebrate species in which laterality establishment was suppressed in viscoelastic fluids and reversed with an artificial flow (Nonaka et al., 2002; Schweickert et al., 2007).
evidence: This incompatibility is based on citations to experimental findings in other species.

claim: A chemosensory mechanism in which a LR gradient is established by combining directional flow around the dorsoventral axis with asymmetric particle secretion in the anterior region could explain the observed robust LR asymmetry establishment, provided that the particle size is above the lower limit of about 2 nm.
source: Finally, we show that a chemosensory mechanism in which a LR gradient is established by combining directional flow around the dorsoventral axis with asymmetric particle secretion in the anterior region could explain the observed robust LR asymmetry establishment, provided that the particle size is above the lower limit of about 2 nm.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion based on computational simulations.

claim: The analysis of physical limitations of two proposed mechanisms rules out directional flow sensing.
source: Although the molecular nature of the flow detection mechanism remains obscure, our analysis of physical limitations of two proposed mechanisms rules out directional flow sensing.
evidence: This conclusion is stated in the Discussion based on the computational modeling results.

claim: The analysis allows prediction of the minimum size of the signaling particle, which will eventually facilitate the search for it.
source: It also allows us to predict the minimum size of the signaling particle, which will eventually facilitate the search for it.
evidence: This prediction is based on the computational simulations of particle diffusion.
